page.layout: Running head at top centre, page number at top left; below them two round woodcut medallions side by side (the legends printed on them are transcribed first); one block of running text, full width, with two paragraphs; below the text a decorative woodcut ornament, not text, so not transcribed.

main_text.p: PERSEVS Iouis filius ex Danaë, Medusam Gorgonem occidit, anno mundi 2497. ante Christum natum 1465. Hic à Græcia in Asiam transfuectus est: ibi Barbaras gentes graui, diuturnóque bello domuit: & nouissimè victor, nomen superatæ genti dedit:nanque à Perseo Persæ dicti sunt. Vide Orof. lib.1.cap.11. De hoc quoq; sic inquit Herodotus lib.7. Posteaquā Perseus ad Cepheum cōmeauit, & Andromedam eius filiam duxit vxorem,tulit ex ea filium,quem Persen appellauit:eúmque illic reliquit (nam Cepheus carebat virili prole) à quo cognomen sortiti sunt Persæ. De Perseo,Poëtæ multi multa fabulantur. Vide Diodo.lib.1.& 4.

ANDROMEDA Cephei regis Aethiopum & Cassiopes filia, vxor fuit Persei, quam scopulo alligatam ac monstro marino, propter matris superbiam, vt aiunt, expositam, liberauit: liberatam in vxorē duxit, occisis Phineo, & reliquis aduersantibus. Acrisiū qui Danaën turri incluserat, occidit Perseus, imprudens tamen. Vide Herodo.lib.7. & Diodorum Siculum multis in locis.

page.notes: The two medallions are woodcut portraits. The legend on the left reads PERSEVS and ARGIVI REX; the legend on the right reads ANDROMEDA and PERS, the last word partly cut off by the medallion edge. The bottom ornament is a decorative woodcut without text. The scan is slightly blurred in the italic line, but the words are legible.
